title: Amazon yeni Fire TV Stick 4K modelini duyurdu
summary: Amazon, Vega işletim sistemini kullanan ve doğrudan televizyonun USB portundan güç alabilen yeni Fire TV Stick 4K modelini satışa sundu.
body:
Amazon yeni Fire TV Stick 4K modelini duyurdu. Pocket-lint ve The Verge gibi teknoloji yayınlarının aktardığına göre cihaz, şirketin Linux tabanlı Vega OS işletim sistemini kullanıyor ve doğrudan televizyonun USB portundan çalışabiliyor.

## Öne çıkan teknik özellikler ve tasarım

Nisan ayında tanıtılan Fire TV Stick HD modeline benzer ince bir tasarımla gelen yeni cihaz, Wi-Fi 6 desteği, 8GB depolama alanı ve dört çekirdekli 1,7 GHz işlemci barındırıyor. HDR10 ve HDR10+ destekleyen cihazda Dolby Vision ile Dolby Atmos özellikleri ise yer almıyor. Önceki Select ve Plus modellerinin yerini alan bu yeni versiyon, kutudan turuncu renkli ana ekran tuşuna ve özelleştirilebilir yıldıza sahip yenilenmiş bir kumandayla çıkıyor.

## Fiyat ve çıkış tarihi

Standart fiyatı 60 dolar olarak belirlenen cihaz, lansmana özel kampanya kapsamında 30 dolardan satışa sunuldu. Yenilenen uzaktan kumanda ise ekim ayının sonlarında 14,99 dolar fiyat etiketiyle ayrı olarak da raflardaki yerini alacak.

**Neden önemli?** Amazon'un gelecekteki tüm yayın cihazlarında Android tabanlı Fire OS yerine Vega OS kullanma stratejisinin bir parçası olan bu yeni model, daha yüksek güç verimliliği ve güvenlik vadediyor.

source_texts.title: Amazon's new $60 4K Fire Stick is shaking things up
source_texts.summary: Amazon has launched a new Fire TV Stick 4K, replacing the Fire TV Stick 4K Select and 4K Plus models.
source_texts.text:
Amazon is making another major change to its Fire TV Stick lineup, just months after launching its new Fire TV Stick HD.
The company announced a new Fire TV Stick 4K launching today, an entry-level 4K streaming stick that will replace not only the Fire TV Stick 4K Select in its lineup but also the Fire TV Stick 4K Plus.
The new Fire TV Stick 4K shares some design similarities with the refreshed Fire TV Stick HD that was released back in April, including a slimmer profile and USB-C. Notably, it can also be powered entirely by your TV's USB port, so you don't need a separate wall plug.
It also comes with a redesigned Fire TV remote, featuring a prominent orange Home button and a customizable Star button you can set to launch any app.
But based on its features, the new Fire TV Stick 4K seems more like a refresh of the 4K Select than of the 4K Plus. It has Wi-Fi 6, 8GB of storage, a quad-core 1.7 GHz processor and supports HDR10 and HDR10+. Unlike the 4K Plus it's replacing, it doesn't support Dolby Vision or Dolby Atmos.
Amazon has priced its new Fire TV Stick 4K at $60, $10 more than the 4K Select and $10 less than the 4K Plus. However, as a special launch promotion, it's available at 50 percent off for $30.
Of course, one of the biggest questions about the new Fire TV Stick 4K is which operating system it uses, and if you've been following Fire TV news lately, you probably won't be surprised by the answer.
The new Fire TV Stick 4K runs Vega OS
Amazon is keeping the Fire TV Stick 4K Max available
Back in April, after launching its refreshed Fire TV Stick HD, Amazon announced that all future Fire TV Sticks would run Vega OS, its new Linux-based operating system. So, unsurprisingly, the new Fire TV Stick 4K runs Vega OS, not Fire OS.
This means that if you want to sideload Android apps or use custom launchers, you can't, since Vega OS is Linux-based.
Amazon has highlighted several reasons for switching to Vega OS on its Fire TV Sticks, including greater efficiency and improved performance, as well as "enhanced security" due to the lack of sideloading. Vega OS's power efficiency also allows the new 4K stick to run off a TV's USB port, something no Android Fire Stick can do.
With the launch of the Fire TV Stick 4K, Amazon is simplifying its Fire TV Stick lineup to just three models again: the Fire TV Stick HD, 4K, and 4K Max. Although the new Fire TV Stick 4K replaces the 4K Select and 4K Plus, Amazon has said both older models will remain available while supplies last.
The Fire TV Stick 4K Max (2nd Gen) is now the oldest in the lineup, released in 2023, and the only Fire TV Stick that still runs Android-based Fire OS.
Pocket-lint asked Amazon whether it also plans to refresh the Fire TV Stick 4K Max soon, but the company declined to comment on future plans.
All in all, if you don't care about Vega OS or Dolby Vision and Atmos and are just looking for a basic 4K streaming stick, the new Fire TV Stick 4K is just that, and its new sleek design and the fact that it can be powered just by a TV's USB port are welcome changes. But if you prefer Fire OS, or want to stream in Dolby Vision and Atmos, the Fire TV Stick 4K Max remains the best option.
The new Fire TV Stick 4K is now available at a temporary discount, down from $60 to $30.

source_texts.text:
The new Fire TV Stick 4K will be a little easier to set up than Amazon’s previous 4K streaming sticks since it no longer requires a power adapter. You can power the device directly from your TV’s USB port, like the updated entry-level Fire TV Stick Amazon launched earlier this year. The Fire TV Stick 4K, available starting today for $59.99, runs on Amazon’s refreshed TV OS and includes Wi-Fi 6, Bluetooth 5.3, and Bluetooth Low Energy.
Amazon’s new Fire TV Stick 4K can pull power directly from your TV
Amazon’s also launching a redesigned Fire TV remote with a new shape and clickier controls.
Amazon’s also simplifying its streaming stick line-up, which now includes four devices instead of five: the Fire TV Stick HD, Fire TV Stick 4K, Fire TV Stick 4K Max, and Fire TV Cube. The new Fire TV Stick 4K is replacing Amazon’s earlier “Select” and “Plus” 4K streaming sticks.
A redesigned Fire TV Remote is launching alongside the new streaming stick, featuring a new asymmetrical shape and “more tactile controls.” The new remote is compatible with all Amazon Ember TVs and Fire TV streaming devices from 2019 onward. It will be available standalone for $14.99 and starts shipping late October. Amazon says it also plans to launch a “Plus” version of the new remote early next year, with an aluminum design, backlit buttons, and a “Find My Remote” feature.
Fire TV is getting a few software updates, as well, including an Alexa Plus Hub and an Alexa Plus integration in the Fire TV mobile app. Amazon says its AI “now draws on real-world context” like awards and events, helping it answer more complex prompts for show and movie suggestions. Amazon Music is also getting a new Fire TV app later this fall, with an Alexa Plus integration users can prompt for music and podcast recommendations.
